snippet.title: Wrapping the off grid cabin.  DIY build part 6
snippet.description:
The rain can be a killer for wood framed buildings.  I move quickly in this video to finish the framing and wrap the whole building in my WRB (weather resistant barrier).  I'm using Protecto Wall VP, from Protecto Wrap.  This is a full-adhered house-wrap.  It is designed to shed liquid water which protects the building during construction, but also long term from any liquid water that gets past the cladding layer.  
The VP stands for Vapor permeable.  This means that water vapor can move through allowing the structure to dry to the outside if conditions allow. 
Also, I add some up-lift resistance down at the beam to joist connection.

snippet.title: Dreame X60 Ultra Robotic Vacuum Review
snippet.description:
Get this robotic vacuum here: https://dreame.shopping/4tJzlcF
Or on Amazon here: https://dreame.shopping/3Ox65X8
There is a Dreame X60 Max Ultra Complete and a X60 Ultra, the two products are very similar. The first one is a 'maxed' out version of the X60 Ultra so it has a few extras like an lifting function that lifts the entire robot for high pile carpets, a baffle the closes for extra suction on carpeted areas, and a dual solution. The 'Complete' part also represents a combination of many useful accessories like extra rollers, brushes, vacuum bags, mops, and solutions. The X60 Ultra is still an excellent robotic vacuum as it was able to vacuum up paper shreds and pet hair with one pass. Be sure to enable the side brush when vacuuming carpet as I show in the video to maximize performance along the edges.

snippet.title: Using an old Light Tower to Charge Off Grid Batteries
snippet.description:
I purchased an old light tower with a diesel generator.  I fixed it, and an testing its fuel economy to recharge my off grid batteries.  When there isn't enough solar energy, I fire up a generator to help.  Let's see how efficient this setup is with Chargeverters.  

The light tower is a Wacker Neuson LTN6.  It has a 6000 Watt generator head (6kVA) paired with a Kohler 1-liter, 3-cylinder, liquid cooled, diesel engine.  The setup should be fairly efficient except for one thing.  The generator head is 120 Volt only.  I would prefer 240V, but lets test this as-is for fuel efficiency.

The light tower was beat up when I bought it, so I removed the lights.  I did maintenance, and replaced the capacitor to get it working.  Now the generator works great.

I have to build a custom extension cord in order to plug in two chargers (100A Chargeverters).  These are made for charging 48V (51.2V) lithium battery banks.
